sources.note: Cursory comparative phonology only. Table 1 (p. 48) 'Phonemic inventories for Bosavi Family languages' gives Agala a supra-segmental column of 'N, LB, OS' (= nasalisation, labialisation, open syllable); p. 49: 'The supra-segmental phonemes of vowel nasalisation and length, and open versus closed syllables, all play a role in the phonemic inventory of the region.' Stress and tone are never mentioned for Agala or any other language; author warns 'the data are too limited to state precise phonological rules'.

sources.note: Section 2.6.2.2.6.5.2 'Agala' (p. 392): 'The only material available in this language is a short word list (unpublished) which shows that it is fairly closely related to Nomad.'
